body: If you want to modify the request data you can use `$this->request->data['field']`, `$this->request->data()` or `$this->request->withData()`. The `withData()` method is what I would recommend as it is not deprecated, but the other forms will continue to exist for the remainder of 3.x.
Closing as there is a pull request open to fix the incorrect documentation.

### What you did
$this->request->data['newKey'] = 'newValue';
Then looked around: https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/10565
used:
$this->request->withData('newKey', 'newValue');

### What happened
It set a new key - value pair - but a NEW copy was created. It did not update the existing one.

### What you expected to happen
Since there is getData() under Request Object, there should be a setData(). When using request->data, it throws a deprecated notice.

### What do you offer
I can send a PR with setData(), point is to over-write the request in-place instead of creating a new one.
